paths.description: Entry/root redirect and primary credential, passkey/social, recovery, invalid-submit, responsive, preference, security, performance and memory surface.

Representative consent and account-creation entry archetype; inspected terms hierarchy, defaults, localization and mobile layout. Successful registration was excluded because it requires identity data and account creation.
Representative account-recovery form; inspected labels, task clarity, localization and mobile layout. Submission was not attempted because it requires personal contact data.
Network/HTTP failure recovery archetype using a deliberately nonexistent route.

findings.summary: The sign-in surface forces the same dark palette regardless of the system colour preference.
findings.evidence: Default/light-condition and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are pixel-identical; the computed root color-scheme is normal and no color-scheme metadata is declared.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark on :root and provide preference-driven light and dark tokens, retaining the current dark palette for dark preference.

findings.summary: Primary action text does not meet WCAG contrast requirements.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 2.99:1 contrast for white text on #05ac4f on the Sign in and Open app controls, below the 4.5:1 requirement for normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the green action surface or use a darker foreground so normal-sized text reaches at least 4.5:1; verify all states.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on the credential fields and several icon controls.
findings.evidence: Programmatic focus inspection reported outline-style none and no box-shadow on both visible credential inputs and three 36px icon buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible outline with adequate offset to every interactive element, including inputs and icon controls.

findings.summary: User zoom is disabled and several text links and icon controls are smaller than 44px.
findings.evidence: All three public flow pages specify maximum-scale=1/user-scalable=no; the target probe found 36x36 icon buttons and multiple links only 15-19px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable restrictions, and enlarge compact controls using padding while preserving the responsive layout.

findings.summary: The mobile sign-in load misses the good LCP range and has a slow visual completion.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.3s, Speed Index 7.7s, and TBT 250ms; the independent trace measured LCP 3.04s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the first-view render, eliminate unnecessary startup assets, and defer non-critical authentication/telemetry modules until needed.

findings.summary: Startup scripting creates avoidable blocking work.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 250ms TBT; the trace found two long tasks up to 93.58ms with 74.23ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Split startup tasks at 50ms boundaries and defer telemetry, CAPTCHA, and passkey work until the relevant interaction.

findings.summary: A simple sign-in view transfers 4.5MB, dominated by four very large font files.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 4,502,020 transferred bytes; fonts accounted for 3,123,898 bytes, four Pretendard weights were 753-779KB each, and two scripts were delivered uncompressed.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset and unicode-range the fonts, load only used weights, compress JavaScript, and add useful immutable caching to versioned static resources.

findings.summary: The entry page ships substantial JavaScript that is unused during the tested load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 268KiB unused JavaScript, including 85.6KB in passkeyApi.js and 62.6KB in appscheme.js.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split passkey, app-scheme, CAPTCHA, and analytics modules and load them only when their associated control or risk state is reached.

findings.summary: Three social sign-in images have no alt attribute or decorative semantics.
findings.evidence: The images primitive and Lighthouse both identified Apple, Google, and LINE SVG images without alt; their parent buttons are named, so the images should be explicitly decorative.
findings.suggestedFix: Add alt="" (or role="presentation") to the decorative images while retaining the accessible name on each parent button.

findings.summary: The authentication origin sets cookies without Secure and weakens its otherwise strong security-header posture.
findings.evidence: Cookie inspection found nid_slevel and NACT without Secure and all seven cookies reported SameSite=None; CSP includes unsafe-inline and Permissions-Policy is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on every HTTPS cookie, use Lax/Strict where cross-site use is unnecessary, remove unsafe-inline through nonce/hash migration, and define a restrictive Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The sign-in page has a broad third-party and telemetry footprint before authentication.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 30 third-party requests and 3,716,277 third-party bytes across eight external origins; several analytics/ad-related Naver origins load on the credential entry view.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise pre-auth telemetry, defer non-essential analytics until consent/context, batch events, and self-host critical assets where practical.

findings.summary: The localized account surfaces do not demonstrate writing-mode-resilient layout primitives.
findings.evidence: The feature probe found no logical CSS properties in accessible stylesheets; the English sign-up DOM also retains Korean heading text in its outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Use inline/block logical properties for spacing and positioning, and ensure hidden/accessibility headings are localized with the visible surface.

findings.summary: The sign-in fields omit standard autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found an empty autocomplete value on both the username/phone input and password input.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete="username" on the identity field and autocomplete="current-password" on the password field; preserve passkey support.

findings.summary: Public account-route changes are abrupt and provide no continuity cue.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules and the three public routes load as unrelated visual states without a directional or shared-element transition.
findings.suggestedFix: Use progressively enhanced cross-document View Transitions for public account navigation while preserving instant navigation where reduced motion is requested.

findings.summary: Font and third-party transfer cost is disproportionate to the small authentication UI.
findings.evidence: A mostly text-and-form page transfers 4.5MB, including 3.12MB of fonts and 3.72MB from third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt a strict pre-auth byte budget, subset fonts, and defer or remove third-party modules that do not support the immediate sign-in task.

findings.summary: The public sign-in document has no meta description.
findings.evidence: DOM, discoverability, and Lighthouse all found a descriptive title but no meta[name=description].
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise localized description explaining that this is NAVER secure sign-in and account access.

findings.summary: The public entry chain has no canonical signal or sitemap endpoint.
findings.evidence: The root redirects three times into a parameterized login URL, DOM inspection found no canonical link, and /sitemap.xml returned 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a stable canonical URL for the public sign-in entry and keep robots/indexing policy consistent with that canonical; add a sitemap only if public account-help routes should be indexed.
